## Active

### D-595 — sport: profile tables share the party PK

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

One human is one core.resource. sport.athlete, sport.coach and sport.specialist use
party.person.personId as their own primary key, so a person holding two roles has two profile rows
and one resource. The cost is that the generic CRUD cannot read or write the person half, so find,
get, add and edit for the five profile tables are custom handlers over two library functions.

### D-596 — sport: person fields flattened into the profile payload

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The athlete, coach, specialist, federation and club models bind one flat master object, so the
person or organisation fields are projected into the profile payload as athlete.firstName and
written back by the profile handler. A nested non-detail object has no persistence in the model
system, which is why the fields are not nested.

### D-597 — sport: competition series and edition are separate tables

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

rules.md requires the type of a sports event and its specific edition to be distinguished and each
edition registered separately. The named recurring competition is sport.competition and a resource;
sport.edition is the time-bound row with year, dates, host and venue. The object is named
competition rather than event because event reads as a log or platform event in the runtime, and the
same type and instance shape then covers award and conferral.

### D-598 — sport: award and conferral are two objects

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

model.md chapter 13 describes one award object, while rules.md requires the award type and a
specific conferral to be separate records. sport.award is the named reusable type with category,
level and conferring body; sport.conferral is the time-bound instance with recipient, date, basis,
document and status. One table would repeat the type attributes on every conferral and break the
single entry rule the model rests on; the cost is one extra model page and one dropdown.

### D-599 — sport: document tables stay generic

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

sport.document and sport.attachment carry no sport specific columns and no sport foreign key to the
document, because they are expected to move into a blong-document realm that is reusable beside
blong-party. Sport only keeps the single document foreign keys on result, qualification, edition and
conferral.

### D-600 — sport: relationship periods are their own models

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

Coaching, support and affiliation periods are edited as their own list pages with athlete, coach and
organisation dropdowns rather than as pivot grids on the athlete page. No realm in the repository
exercises the edge pivot yet, and a list page is honest about what the tables hold.

### D-601 — sport: party.person gains three identity columns

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The model needs the international spelling of the name, the citizenship and a photograph for all
three person roles, so party.person gains internationalName, citizenship and photoUrl. They belong
to the person, not to a role, and the party realm is the only place that keeps them single.

### D-602 — sport: party person label becomes the full name

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

party.person gains a personName column filled with the full name and resource.nameColumn points at
it, so every dropdown and every ACL target shows a full name instead of a surname. There is no
backwards compatibility requirement, so seeds, fixtures and the party screenshots move with the
change. A dev database that already holds persons may need the column added before the sync accepts
it.

### D-603 — sport: classification values are enums, not tables

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

Competition kind, result kind and document type are controlled values declared as widget options,
not classifier tables. Every object name in the runtime is a single word, and these value sets are
short and closed; the columns stay strings so a table can replace the enum later without a
migration.

### D-604 — sport: no fine-grained RBAC in the POC

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The POC declares a permission on every model but seeds no roles, capabilities or actions, and the
dev Admin role holds every action. Fine grained capabilities are deferred until the entity set is
stable.

### D-605 — sport: per-cycle athlete row is called campaign

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The Olympic status and development group of model.md holds one row per athlete per Olympic cycle.
The table is sport.campaign with athleteId, cycleId, olympicStatus, the BOC programme flag, the
Olympic result and the rating fields; campaign reads as the athlete campaign for a cycle rather than
a duplicate of participation.

### D-606 — sport: qualification and quota are one table for now

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

rules.md wants separate records for the qualification achievement, the Olympic quota and the
confirmed right of participation, while model.md describes one object. The POC keeps one
sport.qualification table with quota columns, confirmed with the owner on 2026-10-23, and the quota
card in the model carries a TBD label until the split is decided.

### D-608 — Cards default to half width, tables opt into col-12

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

Deck resolves a column as firstCard.config.className with the fallback col-12 xl:col-6, in both the
flat grid and the tab content, so two cards share a row on xl and a model overrides the width by
declaring className on the card. Every sport model therefore declares no className except the
child-list cards (the athlete results, Olympic status, awards and documents lists and the
competition editions list), which carry col-12 because a table needs the full row.

### D-610 — A model names the layout its Open page renders

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The generated Open page asked the editor for the layout named edit, so a model that declared its
tabs under editThumbIndex never showed them: the page came out as the flat grid. IModelSpec gains
openLayout (default edit) and withDefaults carries it into the resolved spec, which
subjectObjectOpen passes to the editor. The athlete declares openLayout editThumbIndex and keeps
edit flat, because the Playwright create helper fills every field in one pass and cannot walk tabs.

### D-609 — Lossless webp is 76 percent larger here, so PNG stays

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The trial was confounded at first: the total stayed near 15 MB only because two changes cancelled.
Pruning the duplicate captures removed about 7 MB and switching to lossless webp added about 7 MB
back. Measured on the identical capture set, 175 pictures of this UI cost 8847259 bytes as PNG and
15641066 as WebP, so webp is 76 percent larger: lossless webp wins on photographs and loses on the
flat, text-heavy editor screens this realm photographs. The format stays a parameter of the model
helpers and test/sportPlay.ts names it, so the realm runs webp as an explicit trial until the owner
calls it; the recommendation is PNG.

### D-611 — The athlete editor is tabbed on the create page too

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The reviewer saw the athlete editor with tabs on the open page and without them on the create page,
because the create page resolved the flat `edit` grid while the open page asked for a separate
tabbed layout through `openLayout`. Two shapes for one page is a defect in the model, not in the
capture, so `edit` is now the six-tab thumb index and `editSplit` stays as the grid variant. The
cost is that the Playwright create helper must reach fields on tabs that are not mounted yet;
`fillFields` walks the thumb index until the field appears, which keeps one `fields` map able to
span several tabs.

### D-623 — The sport browse shots picture the row their spec created

> _2026-10-25 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The competition and campaign browse shots now run _after_ the create test of the same file and
filter to what it wrote (`searchText: competitionName` / `'ENT-PLAY-OL rating body'`), because
neither table has a seeded row to point at. Before that they were unfiltered, so the baseline was a
picture of whatever the database happened to hold: `sport-competition-browse` carried four
accumulated `ENT-PLAY-CO-…` rows and `sport-campaign-browse` a stale `ENT-PLAY-OL-593990 Athlete`
row, while the CI runner's fresh database produced `No rows.` for the competition shot and a row
from a spec file that happened to run alongside for the campaign one. That is the same trap T-148
records for the marine lists, and the fix is the one `athleteTabs.play.ts` already used in this
realm: photograph the spec's own record, filtered, rather than "the first page of whatever exists".

The filter has to name a stored string column, not a joined label: the search runs over the object's
string properties, so `ratingOrganisationName` narrows the campaign table while the athlete label
shown in it (`ENT-PLAY-OL Athlete`) would not match at all. The cost is a search box that reads
`ENT-PLAY-CP Competition` in an otherwise product-looking picture; the alternative is seeding a
competition and a campaign (the campaign needs an athlete, which is a party person) into a demo
realm whose reference data is deliberately small.

T-412 finished the sweep: federation (`organisations.play.ts`) and coaching and support
(`relationships.play.ts`) had the same shape — browse declared before the create, no seed, so the
baseline was an empty table hiding every column the model declares. All three now create first and
filter by the row's own text (`legalName`, `basisNote`). Five browse shots in this realm follow the
rule; a new spec should start from it rather than from "browse, then create".

### D-637 — The sport deployment entry is the existing index.ts

> _2026-10-27 · realm/blong-sport · active_

index.ts is already the standalone server bootstrap. The loader skips the testRealm child under
release because no testRealm config block is merged into that intent, so the test runner does not
load and no test package is needed in the artifact. A deploy.ts would duplicate the children and the
config for no gain. The suite settings (kustomize.deploy, release, k8s and upgrade) go into
index.ts, and the artifact entry is /opt/deploy/suite/realm/blong-sport/index.ts.

### D-638 — Sport runs as a monolith against the dev cluster external MySQL

> _2026-10-27 · realm/blong-sport · active_

The first deployment is one process (profile monolith) in namespace blong-sport, with the realm
declared as a service and the portal served by that single process. The database is the dev
cluster's existing mysql.blong-integration Service, reached through an ExternalName alias named db,
with a dedicated blong-sport schema and a dedicated blong-sport MySQL user granted all rights on it.
The database must exist before the process connects: MySQL answers Unknown database 'blong-sport'
when the connection names a schema nobody created, and the migration Job fails before it can create
anything. The init script therefore creates the database, the user and the grant, and the same
statements ran once on the running MySQL; the earlier assumption that the seed or migration job
creates the database was wrong. Generating a MySQL through kustomize would add a second database
workload to the dev cluster for one suite.
